findings.title: Out-of-range intensity is clamped to 'Severe' on Home/Calendar and survives the edit screen with nothing selected
findings.eli5: An invalid intensity from a bad backup was shown as 'Severe' on Home and Calendar as if it were real. Fixed at the source: such values can no longer be imported.
findings.what: importEntries only checks `typeof e.intensity === 'number'`, so an out-of-range intensity (e.g. 8) from a backup is inserted as-is; IntensityIcon/intensityColor then clamp it to Severe on Home/Calendar, and the edit screen loads it with no scale button selected yet lets Save re-persist it because the only guard is `intensity === null`.
findings.evidence: app/components/intensity/IntensityIcon.tsx:45 `const Icon = icons[Math.max(0, Math.min(level, 5)) ...]`; app/constants/theme.ts:5 `SCALE_COLORS[Math.max(0, Math.min(v, 5))]`; app/entry/[id].tsx:57 `const selected = value === i;` (i ranges 0–5, so 8 matches nothing) and [id].tsx:254 `if (intensity === null)` is the only save guard, so Save stays enabled and updateEntry writes 8 back. Git: `git log -S'1–10'` finds no entry form with a 10-point scale (f1b5183's add.tsx already used `Array.from({ length: 5 })`), so no legacy source exists other than a hand-edited backup.
findings.goesWrong: Import a backup containing `"intensity": 8`. Home's recent-entries row and the Calendar day cell show the Severe (level 5) icon/colour with no indication the stored value is invalid; opening the entry shows the six scale buttons all unselected; tapping Save without touching intensity keeps 8 in the DB. (The Stats crash from the same row is already catalogued.)
findings.fix: Clamp or reject at the write boundary (importEntries/updateEntry: `Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 0 && v <= 5`), and in the edit screen treat an out-of-range loaded value as null so the user must re-select before saving.

findings.title: Backup omits timezone/local_date/source, so restores re-bucket days in the importing device's zone
findings.eli5: Same as A15: backups lacked time-zone info so restores could move entries to the wrong day. Fixed.
findings.what: importEntries recomputes local_date from the importing device's current timezone (and omits source) because the export payload in app/my-data.tsx:141-151 never carries timezone/local_date/source; restoring a backup on a device in a different zone shifts late-evening/early-morning entries to an adjacent day in the calendar, trend, reports and achievement day counts, and source provenance is replaced by backfillLegacySource's guess on next launch.
findings.evidence: my-data.tsx:141-151 maps each entry to `created_at, intensity, duration, location, pitch, impact, note, tinnitus_types, triggers` — no `timezone`, `local_date` or `source`. queries.ts:341-345: `const timezone = getDeviceTimeZone(); const localDate = computeLocalDate(e.created_at, timezone);` and the INSERT column list excludes `source`, leaving it NULL until the next launch's `backfillLegacySource` (database.ts:141-161) relabels it.
findings.goesWrong: User logs at 23:30 in New York (local_date Oct 4), exports, later moves to London, uses Delete All + Import to restore: local_date becomes Oct 5 for that entry and every other late-evening one. Calendar, day-of-week stats and trigger-day grouping all shift; streak/achievement day counts can change. Entries that were 'scheduled' come back as 'legacy'/'self_initiated'.
findings.fix: Add `timezone` (and `source`) to the export payload and bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`; on import, use the stored timezone for `computeLocalDate` and fall back to the device zone only for version-1 backups.

findings.title: Double-tapping Save inserts the same entry twice
findings.eli5: Same as A14: double-tapping Save created two identical entries. Fixed.
findings.what: handleSave has no re-entry guard and the Save PressableScale (lines 503-507) is never disabled, so a second tap in the 200 ms before router.back() inserts a duplicate entry, double-fires analytics/achievement sync, and queues a second router.back(); app/entry/[id].tsx:253-282/486-490 shares the pattern (idempotent update, but duplicate events and extra back navigation).

findings.title: On iOS the date/time pickers are never dismissed and stay inlined in the layout
findings.eli5: On iPhone, once you open the date or time picker on the entry form it never goes away; it stays stuck on the screen. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: On iOS the date/time pickers are never dismissed: both `onChange` handlers in the shared form set the show flag to `Platform.OS === 'ios'` (always true there) and nothing else sets it false, so the compact native control stays inlined between the header and the ScrollView for the life of the screen. Since the add and edit screens are thin wrappers around one `EntryForm` (app/entry/new.tsx, app/entry/[id].tsx), both screens are affected by the single code path.
findings.evidence: app/components/EntryForm.tsx:460-469: `{showDatePicker && <DateTimePicker value={entryDate} mode="date" maximumDate={new Date()} onChange={(event, selected) => { setShowDatePicker(Platform.OS === 'ios'); ... }} />}` and :471-480 the same for the time picker (`setShowTimePicker(Platform.OS === 'ios')`), no `display` prop and no close/done affordance. `grep -n 'setShowDatePicker(false)\|setShowTimePicker(false)' app/components/EntryForm.tsx` → nothing. @react-native-community/datetimepicker is pinned at 8.6.0 (package.json:14); its iOS `default` display is compact/inline on iOS 14+, i.e. an always-visible control.
findings.goesWrong: iOS user taps the date in the header. An unstyled compact date picker appears above the intensity card and remains there for the life of the screen; tapping the time adds a second one. They cannot be hidden, and they shift the whole form down.
findings.fix: On iOS render the picker inside a modal/bottom sheet with a Done button that sets the show flag to false (or use `display="inline"` inside a dismissible container); on Android keep the current dialog flow.

findings.title: iOS export leaves the full-diary JSON in the cache forever and records 'export completed' even when the user cancels
findings.eli5: Partly fixed. On iPhone, exporting a backup leaves a full plain-text copy of your diary in a temporary folder forever, and the app records 'exported' even if you cancelled.
findings.what: iOS export writes the full diary JSON to Paths.cache and never deletes it (app/my-data.tsx:257-263; unlike reportExport.ts:12-19, which deletes in finally), and then unconditionally sets last_exported_at and logs export_completed (:266-269) even when Sharing.isAvailableAsync() is false or the share sheet is dismissed — the Android branch's `if (!saved) return` guard (:252) has no iOS counterpart.
findings.evidence: app/my-data.tsx:257-263 `const file = new File(Paths.cache, \`tinnitus-tracker-backup-${dateStamp}.json\`); ... file.write(json); if (await Sharing.isAvailableAsync()) { await withSystemUi(() => Sharing.shareAsync(file.uri, ...)); }` — no delete follows (the Android MediaStore path at :109-118 does delete its staged copy). Lines 266-269 then run `setSetting('last_exported_at', now); setLastExported(now); logEvent('export_completed', ...)` regardless. Contrast src/features/reports/reportExport.ts:9-19: 'Keeping reports in cache would leave sensitive health summaries behind with no user-visible way to remove them' + `finally { if (file.exists) file.delete(); }`.
findings.goesWrong: iOS user taps Export, the share sheet opens, they tap Cancel. My Data now shows 'Last exported today' and analytics records a completed export, although no file was saved anywhere the user can find; meanwhile a copy of every entry and note sits in the app cache indefinitely (one file per date).
findings.fix: Delete the cache file after `shareAsync` resolves (or on next launch), and on iOS only set `last_exported_at`/log the event when sharing was actually available; treat `isAvailableAsync() === false` as an error state with a dialog.

findings.title: PDF is deleted the instant the Android chooser returns, before the receiving app has necessarily read it
findings.eli5: Partly fixed. On Android the PDF report is deleted the moment the share menu closes, which can be before the app you shared it to has actually read it, so the attachment may be empty.
findings.what: The report PDF is deleted in `finally` as soon as `Sharing.shareAsync` resolves, but on Android that promise resolves in `OnActivityResult` when the chooser closes (SharingModule.kt:80-84) and the receiver only holds a FileProvider URI to the cache file (no copy, SharingModule.kt:31-49); a target app that reads the stream lazily (on send/upload) gets a missing file. The comment "The receiving app gets its own copy" is incorrect. Defer cleanup (e.g. purge stale report files on next launch / next report creation) instead of deleting synchronously.
findings.evidence: src/features/reports/reportExport.ts:16-20: `finally { if (file.exists) file.delete(); }` right after `await Sharing.shareAsync(...)`. node_modules/expo-sharing/android/src/main/java/expo/modules/sharing/SharingModule.kt:52 `startActivityForResult(intent, REQUEST_CODE)` and :80-83 `OnActivityResult { ... pendingPromise?.resolve(null) }` — the promise resolves on the chooser's result, and the receiver only holds a FileProvider URI granted on line 48-50.
findings.goesWrong: User taps 'Create and Share PDF', picks an app that attaches content URIs lazily (reads the stream when the message/upload is actually sent, or after its compose screen finishes loading). By then `file.delete()` has run and the attachment fails with a 'file not found' / empty attachment. Plausible rather than confirmed on-device — depends on the receiver's read timing.
findings.fix: Defer deletion: e.g. delete stale report files on the next app launch / next report creation, or on `AppState` returning to 'active' after a share, rather than synchronously after `shareAsync` resolves.

findings.title: Report PDF is deleted the instant the Android share chooser hands off, before the target app has read it; cancel still counts as shared
findings.eli5: Partly fixed. Same as A54, plus cancelling the share still counts as 'shared'.
findings.what: On Android the report PDF is deleted in `finally` as soon as `Sharing.shareAsync` resolves, which happens in `OnActivityResult` when the chooser closes — before the target app has read the FileProvider URI — so lazily-reading targets get a missing/empty attachment. On both platforms the promise also resolves on cancel (Android: unconditional in OnActivityResult; iOS: `type == nil && !completed` branch), so `reports.tsx:48` unlocks `first_report` for a dismissed share sheet.
findings.evidence: reportExport.ts:10-19 `await Sharing.shareAsync(result.uri, {...}); return true; } finally { if (file.exists) file.delete(); }`. node_modules/expo-sharing/android/.../SharingModule.kt:52 `startActivityForResult(intent, REQUEST_CODE)` and :80-84 `OnActivityResult { ... pendingPromise?.resolve(null) }` — the chooser finishes as soon as a target is picked (and also on cancel), so the promise cannot distinguish success from dismissal. reports.tsx:48 `if (shared) unlockEvent('first_report');` treats any resolution as a completed share.
findings.goesWrong: Android user taps Create report and picks Google Drive / Gmail / a messaging app. The chooser returns immediately, `file.delete()` runs, and the target app's background read of the FileProvider URI fails with 'file not found' or an empty attachment; the app has already shown success. Separately, a user who opens the chooser and backs out still unlocks the 'first_report' milestone and reports.tsx shows no error.
findings.fix: On Android do not delete immediately: keep the PDF in cache and clean up stale report files on the next app launch or next createAndShareReport call (e.g. delete anything older than a few minutes in a dedicated reports/ cache subfolder); iOS can keep the immediate delete since its completion handler fires after the activity completes. Treat `shareAsync` resolution as 'chooser dismissed', not 'shared': do not unlock first_report from it on Android, or only unlock on iOS where `completed` is reported.

findings.title: `userInterfaceStyle: "light"` is dead config on Android and breaks the Automatic theme on iOS
findings.eli5: Same as A28: the forced light setting breaks automatic dark mode on iPhone and does nothing on Android. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: `userInterfaceStyle: "light"` is a no-op on Android (expo-system-ui not installed) but on iOS prebuild writes `UIUserInterfaceStyle=Light` to Info.plist, forcing `useColorScheme()` to 'light' and making ThemeContext's 'automatic' setting behave as Light. findings.evidence: app.json:9 `"userInterfaceStyle": "light"`. node_modules/@expo/prebuild-config/build/plugins/unversioned/expo-system-ui/withAndroidUserInterfaceStyle.js:16-20 only calls `addWarningAndroid('userInterfaceStyle', 'Install expo-system-ui in your project to enable this feature.')`; `ls node_modules/expo-system-ui` -> not installed. withIosUserInterfaceStyle.js:22,28-29 maps it to the Info.plist key; the locally generated ios/TinnitusTracker/Info.plist:88-89 contains `<key>UIUserInterfaceStyle</key><string>Light</string>`. app/contexts/ThemeContext.tsx:26 `const systemScheme = useColorScheme();` and :33 `setting === 'automatic' ? (systemScheme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light') : setting`.
findings.goesWrong: On iOS (planned per backlog) a user with system dark mode leaves the theme on the default 'automatic' and always gets the light theme; the Appearance screen's Automatic option is silently non-functional. On Android the setting does nothing, so it misleads whoever reads app.json into thinking the system scheme is intentionally suppressed.
findings.fix: Set `"userInterfaceStyle": "automatic"` (the value the ThemeContext design assumes) and keep expo-system-ui uninstalled, or remove the key.

findings.title: Guide says no direction is named when the 95% range crosses zero; the Trigger Impact panel names one at 60% probability regardless

(es.ts:16 '…cruza cero… la app no añade una dirección', de.ts:16 '…die App nennt dann keine Richtung') vs app/(tabs)/trends.tsx:324-331 — `prob >= 0.6 ? { color: worse ? 'stats.trigger.probWorse' : 'stats.trigger.probBetter', { percent })` with `prob = Math.max(data.probWorse, data.probBetter)` (:283); the comment at :299-302 ('The direction is only named when the whole interval sits on one side of zero') describes the ciLine block :303-312. The PDF repeats the 0.6 rule at reportHtml.ts:119-120.
findings.goesWrong: A trigger with posterior effect +0.6 and SE 0.35: probWorse = 1 - Φ((0.5-0.6)/0.35) ≈ 0.61 >= 0.6, so the panel prints '61% likely to be meaningfully worse' in the worse colour, while ciLow = 0.6 - 1.96*0.35 ≈ -0.09 < 0, i.e. the range crosses zero. findings.title: The ridge penalty and posterior variance use the marginal variance of intensity, not the residual variance, so the stated prior SD of 0.35 and the '95% range' describe a model that only runs when triggers explain nothing
findings.eli5: Still open. A technical detail in the statistics model: it measures 'noise' in a way that makes it too cautious when a trigger really matters, so a real effect can be shrunk and its uncertainty overstated.
findings.what: sigma2 (triggerModel.ts:204) is the marginal variance of intensity, not residual noise, yet it is used both as the ridge scale (:209, λ = Var(y)/0.35²) and as the posterior-variance scale (:266). Whenever triggers explain real variance the effective prior is tighter than the 0.35 stated in src/features/statistics/guides/en.ts:73 and the intervals wider than the ±1.96 SE described at :75 (same text in guides/de.ts:26/28, es.ts:26/28, fr.ts:26/28) — conservative in direction, but the technical guide documents a model that is only run when triggers explain nothing. Either re-estimate σ² from residuals (effective df) and refit penalty + inverse together, or amend the guide text.
findings.evidence: triggerModel.ts:203-205: `sigma2 = Σ(v - yMean)² / (n-1)` from the raw outcome; :209 `ridge = new Array(p).fill(sigma2 / (PRIOR_SD * PRIOR_SD))`; :266 `const v = sigma2 * inv[col][col]`. With λ = Var(y)/τ², the implied prior SD is τ·sqrt(σ²_resid/Var(y)). The author's own comment :244-251 says a future noise update 'must refit both the penalty and inverse together'. guides/en.ts:73 states 'standard deviation of 0.35 intensity levels' and :75 'The 95% range is the estimate plus or minus 1.96 model-based standard errors'. tests/stats/calibration.test.ts:206-208 admits 'The model is often conservative (observed truth rates exceed stated probabilities)'. tests/stats/triggerModel.validation.ts:64 only asserts the trivially-satisfied prior-width bound.
findings.goesWrong: A user whose one real trigger explains ~50% of day-to-day variance: the effect is shrunk as if the prior SD were ~0.25 and the interval is computed with a doubled noise variance, so a true +1.0-level trigger reads as roughly +0.6 with a wide bar and the 'likely to be meaningfully worse' label arrives weeks later than the data supports; the technical guide tells them a different model was used.
findings.fix: After the first solve, estimate σ² from residuals with effective degrees of freedom (n − trace of the hat matrix), rebuild the ridge and re-solve once (one extra closed-form pass), or keep the current conservative choice and state in the guide that the penalty is scaled by the total variance of intensity.

'one' : 'other'` dummyRule for every language. Result: Slavic/Baltic/Romanian users get grammatically wrong strings for most counts (e.g. ru.json:559 `_other` "записей" used for 2-4) in My Data, Reports, Profile and Learn.
findings.evidence: Per-locale plural-suffix scan at HEAD: en/de/es/fr/… {one:11, other:10-11, zero:1}; cs/sk/pl/lt {one, few, many, other: 11 each}; ru/uk {few:4, many:4}; hr/sr/ro {few:4}; sl {two:4, few:4}; lv {zero:11}. Keys: learn.minutes, myData.{dataDeletedMessage,daysAgo,entriesLogged,importCompleteMessage,importSkippedEntries,importSkippedLinks}, personalization.activeCount, reports.notesInPeriod, reports.pdf.answeredEntries, stats.trigger.dayCount. Runtime: `strings` on ios/Pods/hermes-engine/.../ios-arm64/hermesvm.framework/hermesvm → DateTimeFormat 12, NumberFormat 13, PluralRules 0, DisplayNames 0; package.json has no intl-pluralrules polyfill and app/i18n/index.ts:39-73 sets no `compatibilityJSON`. i18next 26.3.6 (node_modules/i18next/dist/cjs/i18next.js:1063-1071): `rule = new Intl.PluralRules(...)` throws → `return dummyRule` where :1035 `dummyRule = { select: count => count === 1 ? 'one' : 'other' }`. Call sites: app/my-data.tsx:92,328-335,363,385, app/reports.tsx:142,162, app/profile.tsx, app/learn/index.tsx.
findings.goesWrong: Russian user with 2 entries opens My Data → header reads "2 записей добавлено" (genitive plural; correct is "2 записи"); Czech Profile with 3 active sound types → "3 aktivních" instead of "3 aktivní"; Polish with 22 entries → "22 wpisów" instead of "22 wpisy". If an Intl.PluralRules polyfill is later added without adding the forms, the resolver (i18next.js:830-865) tries `key_few`, then the bare key, then moves to the `en` fallback where the suffix is recomputed as `_other` — a Russian user with 5 entries would then see the English "5 entries logged".
findings.fix: Do both halves: (1) import an Intl.PluralRules polyfill (e.g. `@formatjs/intl-pluralrules` + locale data for the 28 languages) before `i18n.init`; (2) add `_few`/`_many` (ru, uk, pl, cs, sk, hr, sr, lt), `_two`+`_few` (sl), `_few` (ro) and `_zero` (lv) variants for `myData.entriesLogged`, `myData.daysAgo`, `myData.importCompleteMessage`, `myData.dataDeletedMessage`, `personalization.activeCount`, `learn.minutes`. Also add a bare base key for each (the same-language safety net `stats.trigger.dayCount` already relies on), and a script that asserts every plural key has all CLDR categories per locale.

findings.title: Thirteen useMemos depend on i18n label arrays that are new objects on every render, so they recompute on every tap/toggle regardless of the fingerprint optimisation
findings.eli5: Same as A23: the Stats screen redoes heavy calculations on every tap because some lists are recreated each time. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: The five i18n label arrays (l.1497-1501) are rebuilt on every StatsScreen render (i18next returnObjects allocates a fresh array; distressLabels is a literal), so the 13 useMemos that list them as deps (l.1547-1562: dowBuckets, four dow enum buckets, four enum period datasets, four smoothed enum trends) recompute on every local state change — trigger-row tap, bars/line toggle, day-of-week category switch — bypassing the fingerprint optimisation. Fix: wrap each label array in useMemo keyed on t / i18n.language.
findings.evidence: trends.tsx l.1497-1501: `const dowLabels = t('stats.dowLabels', { returnObjects: true }) as string[];` (same for pitch/duration/location) and `const distressLabels = [t(...), t(...), t(...)]`. i18next builds a new container per call: node_modules/i18next/dist/esm/i18next.js l.628 `const copy = resTypeIsArray ? [] : {};` ... l.655 `res = copy;`. Those arrays are deps of dowBuckets (l.1547), dowPitch/dowDuration/dowLocation/dowDistress (l.1549-1552), pitchData..distressData (l.1553-1556) and pitchTrend..distressTrend (l.1559-1562). computeDayOfWeekBuckets constructs a Date per entry (l.784) and smoothStackedTrend runs four rolling passes.

findings.fix: Memoise the label arrays on the i18n language: `const dowLabels = useMemo(() => t('stats.dowLabels', { returnObjects: true }) as string[], [t])` (and the same for the others, including distressLabels), or compute buckets with stable keys and attach labels at render time.

findings.title: Custom tab bar buttons discard the accessibility props react-navigation supplies; the Add FAB is an unlabeled icon-only control
findings.eli5: The custom tab bar throws away the accessibility information for the four main tabs, so screen readers do not say 'tab' or 'selected'. Only the + button was fixed. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: `TabBarButton` (line 21/33) forwards only onPress/onLongPress/style, dropping the navigator's `role`, `aria-selected`, `aria-label`, `testID` and `android_ripple`, so the four regular tabs lose their tab role and selected state for screen readers. The Add FAB itself is now labelled (`AddTabButton` at :44-101 passes `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityLabel={t('tabs.add')}` and the navigator's `accessibilityState`), so only the regular tabs remain affected. `tabBarIcon` on line 155 is still dead code.
findings.evidence: _layout.tsx:21 `function TabBarButton({ children, onPress, onLongPress, style }: BottomTabBarButtonProps)` and :33 `<Pressable onPress={onPress} onLongPress={onLongPress} onPressIn={onPressIn} onPressOut={onPressOut} style={style}>` — nothing else is forwarded. :44 `function AddTabButton({ accessibilityState }: BottomTabBarButtonProps)` and :94-100 `<PressableScale ... accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel={t('tabs.add')} accessibilityState={accessibilityState}>` (fixed). :155 `tabBarIcon: () => <Plus .../>` on the add screen is never rendered because the custom button ignores `children`.
findings.goesWrong: TalkBack/VoiceOver user swipes across the tab bar: Home/Stats/Calendar/More announce without the tab role or "selected" state; the Add FAB announces as "button" (or nothing) with no name, so the primary action of the app is undiscoverable non-visually. Automated UI tests also cannot target tabs by `testID`.
findings.fix: In `TabBarButton`, destructure `...rest` and spread it onto `Pressable`. In `AddTabButton`, forward `props['aria-label']`/`testID` (or set `accessibilityRole="button"` and `accessibilityLabel={t('tabs.add')}` explicitly) on the `PressableScale`, and remove the unused `tabBarIcon` for the add screen.

findings.what: Stat tiles (index.tsx:504-531, trends.tsx:2250-2275) and the tab bar (_layout.tsx:131) use fixed pixel heights around 10-12pt text with no allowFontScaling/maxFontSizeMultiplier anywhere in the app, so at large OS accessibility text sizes labels and captions overflow their rows and overlap neighbouring content. The entry-form scale buttons (IntensityScaleSelector.tsx:95-97) are a fixed 66px tall with a 20px label line clamped to one line, so a scaled label truncates rather than wraps.

findings.fix: Replace fixed heights with minHeight, set `maxFontSizeMultiplier={1.4}` on the dense tiles/tab labels, and raise 9–10pt styles to ≥11pt.

findings.title: No data-access layer: screens call SQLite directly in render/focus, duplicate derived facts, and pass state through a module-level global
findings.eli5: Still open. Every screen talks to the database on its own, in its own way, so facts like 'logged today?' are computed in several places and can disagree.
findings.what: No data-access layer: 34 files outside app/db import queries.ts directly, every screen hand-rolls fetch-on-focus (trends.tsx adds its own fingerprint cache, calendar.tsx double-queries each month change at :147-149 plus :178/:187), the 'logged today?' fact is computed from two separate queries (_layout.tsx:16-18 and index.tsx:127-130, the former running a synchronous SQLite read inside render on every pathname change), and calendarNav.ts:7 uses a mutable module global to hand a date between screens because no shared store exists. Not a user-visible bug today — focus refetches keep data fresh — but each new consumer re-implements the pattern and the workarounds keep accumulating.
findings.evidence: (tabs)/_layout.tsx:16-18 `getRecentEntries(50).some(e => e.local_date === todayStr)` called from :49-50 `usePathname(); const remind = !hasEntryToday();` i.e. a DB read inside render on every navigation; app/(tabs)/index.tsx:127-130 recomputes the same from its own `getRecentEntries(200)` (:107/:117). Focus refetches: index.tsx:114-121, trends.tsx:1593-1601 (fingerprintStatsInput :75), calendar.tsx:118-146 (+ :147-149 `[monthKey]` effect and :178/:187 direct calls → double-fetch per month change), more.tsx:109-111, profile.tsx:52-58, my-data.tsx, reports.tsx, achievements.tsx. app/utils/calendarNav.ts:7 `let pendingCalendarDate: string | null = null;` with the 6-line comment explaining why. ExpandableEntryRow.tsx:56,124 issues two more queries per expanded row. `grep -rl db/queries app src | grep -v app/db/ | wc -l` → 34.
findings.goesWrong: Adding any screen that shows entries means re-implementing fetch+focus+fingerprint; a change made on one screen is only visible on another after a focus event (e.g. More's milestone badge, Profile's active counts); the Add FAB re-queries 50 rows on every push/pop including Settings sub-screens; cross-screen hand-offs keep growing ad-hoc globals.
findings.fix: Introduce a thin repository + hook layer over queries.ts (e.g. `useEntries(range)`, `useTodayLogged()`, `useSettings()`) backed by a tiny event bus or TanStack Query with explicit invalidation on saveEntry/updateEntry/deleteEntry/import/deleteAll; keep screens free of db imports.

findings.title: Home computes its 7-day stats from a 200-row cap while Stats uses 1000, so the two can disagree despite the comment promising they cannot

findings.what: Home computes its 7-day change/leading-value stats from getRecentEntries(200) (a row cap, not a 14-day date window) while Stats uses getRecentEntries(1000); for a user with >~14 entries/day the previous-week window is truncated on Home only, so the Change tile can disagree with Stats despite the comment at index.tsx:105-107 claiming they cannot. Fetch by local_date (today-13 onward) or match the Stats cap.
findings.evidence: index.tsx:88 and :92 `getRecentEntries(200)`; index.tsx:105-107 comment: "built from the same shared functions ... so the two screens can never disagree about what 'this week' means". trends.tsx:1484 `getRecentEntries(1000)`. queries.ts:209-213 `SELECT * FROM entries ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?`. sevenDayTrend.ts:306-315 `periodAverages` filters `p.tsList` for days -13..-7; :400 `computeLeadingValue` filters for `e.day < windowStartDayStr`.
findings.goesWrong: User averaging 15+ entries/day (several self-initiated check-ins plus the scheduled prompt), or who imported a dense backup: 200 rows cover ~13 days, so Home's previous-week average is computed from a partial window (or is null) while Stats 7D shows the full comparison — the Change tile differs between the two screens.
findings.fix: Fetch by date for this screen (e.g. `WHERE local_date >= ?` with today-13 as the key, no LIMIT), or raise the cap to match Stats. Keep the 20-row list slice separate from the stats input.

findings.title: Eight context providers re-implement the same get/setSetting boilerplate and nest eight deep
findings.eli5: Still open. Eight settings are each wrapped in their own nearly identical code layer; adding a new setting means copying it all again.
findings.what: Theme, ChartType, FirstDayOfWeek, IntensityScale and Language contexts duplicate the same validated getSetting/setSetting useState boilerplate (ThemeContext.tsx:27-30, ChartTypeContext.tsx:29-31, FirstDayOfWeekContext.tsx:35-37, IntensityScaleContext.tsx:25-27, LanguageContext.tsx:77-80) and are stacked as eight nested providers in app/_layout.tsx:184-191; a small shared `usePersistedSetting(key, allowed, default)` hook would remove the repetition. The claimed render cascade across providers does not occur: each provider's stable `children` element prevents re-rendering sibling contexts' consumers, so the unmemoised value literals only matter when that setting itself changes.
findings.evidence: app/_layout.tsx:184-191 eight nested providers (Onboarding, Subscription, IntensityScale, ChartType, FirstDayOfWeek, Language, Theme, AppLock). Identical shape in ThemeContext.tsx:27-30, ChartTypeContext.tsx:29-31, FirstDayOfWeekContext.tsx:35-37, IntensityScaleContext.tsx:25-27, LanguageContext.tsx:77-80 (`const saved = getSetting('...'); return (ALL_SETTINGS as string[]).includes(saved ?? '') ? ... : default`), plus OnboardingContext.tsx:17, AppLockContext.tsx:26-27, SubscriptionContext.tsx:45. Context values are fresh object literals (ThemeContext.tsx:45, LanguageContext.tsx:103, ChartTypeContext.tsx:42, etc.).
findings.goesWrong: Each new preference (e.g. a planned analytics opt-out) costs a new context file, a provider edit in _layout.tsx, a settings screen and a Settings row; reading `useTheme()` in ~40 components means every provider re-render re-renders all of them because the value identity changes.

findings.title: "Today" is captured at render time on both tab screens, so neither notices a date rollover while it is on screen
findings.eli5: The Home and Calendar tabs decide what 'today' is when they are drawn and do not notice midnight passing, so after midnight you may be told you cannot log 'future' days. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: Calendar's `todayStr` (calendar.tsx:78-79) and Home's `hasEntryToday` (index.tsx:127-130) are computed from `new Date()` at render/memo time and only refreshed by a navigation focus event; the tab screens stay mounted and nothing listens to AppState, so after a date rollover while the app sits on the tab (or is backgrounded, with or without App Lock — the LockScreen is now an overlay above the navigator, so a re-lock no longer remounts the tabs and no longer masks this) the new day is treated as "future" on Calendar and Home keeps hiding the Log CTA/subline until the user switches tabs.
findings.evidence: calendar.tsx:78-79 `const today = new Date(); const todayStr = toLocalDateStr(today);` used by the guard at :196 `if (dateStr > todayStr) { showFutureToast(); return; }` and :270 `const isFuture = dateStr > todayStr;`. index.tsx:127-130 `const hasEntryToday = useMemo(() => { const todayStr = formatDateKey(new Date()); return entries.some(...); }, [entries]);` gates the subline at :194 and the CTA at :224. Neither screen subscribes to `AppState`. app/_layout.tsx:146 `{locked && <LockScreen style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill} />}` — an overlay, so the tab state survives a lock (CLAUDE.md 2026-10-14, A2/A7).
findings.goesWrong: User leaves the app on the Calendar tab at 23:55, locks the phone, unlocks at 00:10: tapping the new day's cell shows "Can't log entries for future days". Same cycle on Home with an entry logged the previous evening: "Log for Today" stays hidden and the "How are you feeling today?" subline is missing until the user switches tabs and back.
findings.fix: Keep a `todayKey` in state refreshed from an `AppState` 'active' listener (and in the focus effect), and derive `todayStr`/`hasEntryToday` from it; or at minimum recompute inside the focus effect and the 'active' transition.

findings.title: Pending-date focus branch leaves `skipFocusResetRef` armed, so the next ordinary tab return skips the snap-to-today once
findings.eli5: A small navigation glitch: after deleting an entry from the Calendar, the next time you return to the Calendar tab it may not jump back to the current month as usual. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: After a delete on the edit screen (which hands the day back via `setPendingCalendarDate` and returns with `router.dismissTo('/(tabs)/calendar')`, so the Calendar instance survives), the pending-date focus branch returns at line 130 without clearing `skipFocusResetRef` (set by `onEditPress` at line 345 before every edit push), so the next ordinary Calendar tab focus skips the snap-to-current-month once.
findings.evidence: calendar.tsx:345 `onEditPress={() => { skipFocusResetRef.current = true; }}` runs before every edit push. entry/[id].tsx:66-68 on delete: `if (entry) setPendingCalendarDate(entry.local_date); router.dismissTo('/(tabs)/calendar');`. calendar.tsx:124-130: `const pendingDate = consumePendingCalendarDate(); if (pendingDate) { ...setState...; return; }` — no `skipFocusResetRef.current = false`. findings.title: "Yesterday" is derived by subtracting 24 h, which is not one calendar day across a DST change
findings.eli5: 'Yesterday' is calculated as 'now minus 24 hours', which is wrong for one hour after a daylight-saving change. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: `formatEntryDate` derives the "Yesterday" key by subtracting 24 h from now and formatting in the local zone; during the first hour after midnight following a spring-forward day this yields two days back, so yesterday's entries show a full date label instead of "Yesterday". Fall-back days are unaffected. Use `d.setDate(d.getDate() - 1)` like sevenDayTrend.ts does.
findings.evidence: index.tsx:48 `const yesterday = formatDateKey(new Date(Date.now() - 86400000));` compared at line 51 `if (entry.local_date === yesterday)`. Every other window computation in the same pipeline uses calendar arithmetic instead (sevenDayTrend.ts:62 `cutoff.setDate(cutoff.getDate() - (days - 1))`, :130, :309-311).
findings.goesWrong: Monday 00:30 local, the day after a spring-forward Sunday (23 h long): 00:30 minus 24 h = Saturday 23:30, so `yesterday` = Saturday. An entry logged Sunday 21:00 renders as "Sun, Mar 8 · 21:00" instead of "Yesterday · 21:00" until 01:00.
findings.fix: `const d = new Date(); d.setDate(d.getDate() - 1); const yesterday = formatDateKey(d);` — same idiom the rest of the stats code already uses.

findings.title: Greeting is computed once per mount and never refreshes with the time of day
findings.eli5: The 'Good morning' greeting is set once when the app opens and never changes, so it can still say 'Good morning' at 7 pm. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: Time-of-day greeting is memoized on `[t]` only (line 96) while `greeting()` reads the clock (line 36); since the Home tab never unmounts and no focus/AppState hook recomputes it, the greeting stays at whatever period the app was first opened in until a restart or language change.
findings.evidence: index.tsx:96 `const greet = useMemo(() => greeting(t), [t]);` — `greeting()` reads `new Date().getHours()` (line 36). `t` from react-i18next is referentially stable until the language changes. Lines 111-113 state: "Home's tab screen stays mounted for the app's whole lifetime (bottom tabs don't unmount on switch), so the useState initializer above only ever ran once". The focus effect (lines 89-94) re-renders the screen but a `[t]`-keyed memo does not recompute.
findings.goesWrong: User opens the app at 11:50 -> headline reads "Good morning, Alex". They background it and return at 15:00 (process still alive), switch tabs and come back -> headline still reads "Good morning, Alex" until the app is killed or the language is changed.
findings.fix: Drop the memo (it is a trivial computation) or recompute it inside the existing `useFocusEffect` callback, e.g. keep `greet` in state and set it alongside `setUserName`/`setEntries`. Pair with an `AppState` -> 'active' refresh if you also want it correct after a background/foreground without a tab switch.

findings.title: Startup DB initialisation has no error path: a failing migration crashes the app without being reported
findings.eli5: Same as A36: a database failure at startup crashes the app with no message or report. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: initDatabase() (migrations, backfills, seeds) runs inside try/finally with no catch at app/_layout.tsx:162-175, unlike the adjacent initPurchases call (:156-160) that routes errors to recordError. A SQLite failure at startup escapes the effect, unmounts the root tree (no ErrorBoundary anywhere in app/), and crashes the app on every launch with no user-facing message or recovery path. Crashlytics' global JS handler would still log the fatal in release builds (only for users who granted usage-data consent), but without the context breadcrumb and with no way for the user to export data or escape the crash loop.
findings.evidence: app/_layout.tsx:162-175 `try { initDatabase(); applyUsageConsent(); const reminders = getReminders(); ... } finally { setAppReady(true); }` — no catch; `recordError` is imported at :12 but only used for initPurchases (:159). `grep -rn ErrorBoundary app src` -> nothing.
findings.goesWrong: A disk-full device or a future migration bug (e.g. ensureColumn on a locked DB) throws on launch -> immediate crash on every start with no breadcrumb in Crashlytics and no user-facing message.
findings.fix: Add a catch that calls recordError(err, 'initDatabase failed') and renders a minimal error screen with a 'Send report / Export data' option instead of a crash loop.

findings.title: Name uniqueness is case-sensitive in the schema but case-insensitive in the add path
findings.eli5: The database treats 'dehydration' and 'Dehydration' as two different names, but the 'add trigger' code treats them as the same, so a future built-in trigger could appear twice next to a user's custom one. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: `tinnitus_types.name` (database.ts:15) and `triggers.name` (database.ts:22) are `UNIQUE` under default BINARY collation, while `addCustomTinnitusType`/`addCustomTrigger` (queries.ts:124, :162) dedupe with `COLLATE NOCASE`. The seed functions' `INSERT OR IGNORE` (database.ts:198-203, 233-238) therefore will not match a pre-existing custom row that differs only by case, so a built-in added in a later update can coexist with the user's custom spelling as two active chips with separate histories. Fix: declare `UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE` for new installs and have the seed functions check `name = ? COLLATE NOCASE` before inserting on existing DBs.
findings.evidence: database.ts:15 and :22 `name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` (case-sensitive by default); seeds use `INSERT OR IGNORE` with exact names (database.ts:198-203, 233-238) and new built-ins are added over time (e.g. `splitPulsatileThrummingType` + 'Thrumming', lines 172-184 and :193). queries.ts:124 and :162 check `WHERE name = ? COLLATE NOCASE` before inserting a custom row.
findings.goesWrong: User adds custom trigger 'dehydration'. A later app update adds built-in 'Dehydration' to `seedTriggers`; `INSERT OR IGNORE` does not match the lowercase row, so both rows exist and the entry form shows two near-identical chips whose histories never merge.
findings.fix: Declare `name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE` for new installs and make the seed functions check `COLLATE NOCASE` before inserting on existing ones.

findings.title: Pulsatile/Thrumming split migration no-ops if the user already created a custom 'Pulsatile', leaving the combined built-in row forever
findings.eli5: The upgrade that split 'Pulsatile / Thrumming' into two sound types does nothing if the user had already created their own 'Pulsatile', leaving the old combined entry stuck forever. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: splitPulsatileThrummingType() returns early when any row named exactly 'Pulsatile' already exists, leaving the built-in 'Pulsatile / Thrumming' row in place (non-deletable, is_custom = 0) next to the user's custom 'Pulsatile' and the newly seeded 'Thrumming'; the user can only hide it by disabling it, not remove or merge it. The exact-match check also diverges from addCustomTinnitusType's COLLATE NOCASE lookup, so a custom 'pulsatile' ends up alongside a renamed built-in 'Pulsatile'.
findings.evidence: app/db/database.ts:174-177 `const pulsatileExists = db.getFirstSync("SELECT id FROM tinnitus_types WHERE name = 'Pulsatile'"); if (pulsatileExists) return;` — the combined row is neither renamed nor retired. Custom sound types shipped in 3fb17d1 (2026-09-21, part of 1.1.0, app.json bumped at c183571 2026-09-14), the split landed later in bad1cb3, so this is a real upgrade path. Lookup is case-sensitive (`name = 'Pulsatile'`) while app/db/queries.ts:124 adds customs with `COLLATE NOCASE`, so a custom 'pulsatile' does not block the rename and yields 'pulsatile' (custom) plus 'Pulsatile' (built-in) side by side.
findings.goesWrong: User on 1.1.0 adds custom sound type 'Pulsatile' (allowed, since the built-in was 'Pulsatile / Thrumming'), logs entries with it, then updates. Sound Types screen now lists 'Pulsatile' (custom), 'Pulsatile / Thrumming' (built-in, cannot be deleted, still attached to old entries) and 'Thrumming'; the entry form shows both Pulsatile variants as chips.
findings.fix: When a 'Pulsatile' row already exists, re-point `entry_tinnitus_types.tinnitus_type_id` from the combined row to it (INSERT OR IGNORE then DELETE the combined row), or at least mark the combined row `is_active = 0`; use COLLATE NOCASE in the existence check to match addCustomTinnitusType.

findings.title: Entry save has no error path: a failed SQLite write throws inside the press handler and crashes the app with no message
findings.eli5: If saving an entry fails (for example the phone is out of storage), the app crashes instead of showing an error, and what you typed is lost. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: handleSave in app/entry/new.tsx (saveEntry, line 27) and app/entry/[id].tsx (updateEntry, line 41) call synchronous runSync writes directly from the form's onSave with no try/catch and no error boundary anywhere in the app; a SQLite failure (disk full, locked DB) throws out of the press handler, crashes a release build, loses the form input and is never reported via recordError. The writes themselves are now wrapped in `db.withTransactionSync` (queries.ts:614, :289), so a half-written entry is no longer possible — the crash and the lost input are.
findings.evidence: new.tsx:27-38 `saveEntry({...})` followed by :39-42 analytics/achievements/widget/reminder calls with no try/catch; [id].tsx:41-52 `updateEntry(Number(id), {...})` likewise; EntryForm.tsx:393-408 calls `onSave(...)` then `setSaved(true); setTimeout(exit, 200)` unguarded. queries.ts:594-614 `export function saveEntry(...) { ... db.withTransactionSync(() => {` and :260-289 for updateEntry. Contrast my-data.tsx `catch (err) { recordError(err, 'export failed'); setStatus({ variant: 'error', ... }) }`. `grep -rn ErrorBoundary app src` → nothing.
findings.goesWrong: Device storage full (SQLITE_FULL) or a locked database: tapping Save throws from the event handler; in a release build the JS exception terminates the app, the user's form input is lost, and nothing is reported to Crashlytics as a handled error.
findings.fix: Wrap the write in try/catch, recordError, and show a StatusDialog with a retry; keep the form state intact.

findings.title: Keyboard overlap subtracts the bottom safe-area inset on iOS too, over-lifting the footer

findings.what: useKeyboardOverlap subtracts insets.bottom from the keyboard top on all platforms, but iOS's endCoordinates.height already reaches the screen bottom; on a home-indicator iPhone the entry screens' sticky footer is lifted ~34 pt above the keyboard, leaving a visible background gap. findings.fix: Use `e.endCoordinates.screenY` as the keyboard top (available on both platforms) or only subtract `insets.bottom` when `Platform.OS === 'android'`.

findings.what: `Linking.openURL` is called without await/catch here and in five other screens (about.tsx:14, connect.tsx:43, support.tsx:54, support-directory.tsx:139, (tabs)/more.tsx:133); only support-directory.tsx:73-79 handles rejection with an error dialog, so elsewhere a failed open is silent (and logs an unhandled rejection in dev).

findings.title: rangeDayCount('All') counts days from a UTC instant while every other Stats figure uses local day keys, so the Entries tile can read '2 of 1 days'
findings.eli5: The 'of N days' number under 'All' is calculated from elapsed hours instead of calendar days, so it can be off by one (even '2 of 1 days'). Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: rangeDayCount('All') rounds the elapsed milliseconds since the oldest created_at (UTC instant) to whole days instead of counting local calendar days from oldestDay, so the Stats Entries tile's "of N days" can be one day too low or too high (e.g. oldest entry yesterday 13:00 viewed today 00:30 → "of 1 days" for a two-day diary), inconsistent with every other Stats figure which uses local_date keys. Only the "All" range on the Stats tab is affected; Home always uses '7D'.
findings.evidence: l.300 `Math.max(1, Math.round((Date.now() - p.oldestTs) / 86400000) + 1)`; oldestTs is `new Date(e.created_at).getTime()` (l.34-37) whereas filterItems (l.64), buckets (l.117) and the model use `e.day` = local_date.
findings.goesWrong: Entries at 23:30 yesterday and 00:30 today (two local days): elapsed = 1h → round(0.04) + 1 = 1 → tile shows '2 of 1 days'. Over a long diary the UTC/local offset and DST shifts can also make it one day off.
findings.fix: Compute the span from `p.oldestDay` to today's local key: `daysBetween(oldestDay, formatDateKey(new Date())) + 1`.

findings.title: Overlapping syncReminderNotifications calls interleave cancel-all/schedule and produce duplicate notifications
findings.eli5: If reminders are changed quickly twice in a row, the two updates can overlap and leave duplicate or wrong notifications scheduled. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: syncReminderNotifications (cancel-all then re-schedule, plus re-arming the anchor) is never serialized and is called fire-and-forget without .catch from app/reminders.tsx:98 (via refreshAndSync), :92, app/components/ReminderPromptHost.tsx:65 and app/_layout.tsx:170; two overlapping runs (rapid toggles, or a toggle during the startup sync) each schedule every reminder and the anchor after both cancels, yielding duplicate daily notifications that nothing can detect since no ids are persisted, and any native rejection is silently swallowed.
findings.evidence: app/utils/notifications.ts:156 `await Notifications.cancelAllScheduledNotificationsAsync();` followed by a sequential `await scheduleNotificationAsync` per enabled reminder (:158-172) and `await rearmPendingAnchor(t)` (:176) with no mutex. app/reminders.tsx:96-99 `function refreshAndSync(next) { setReminders(next); syncReminderNotifications(next, t); }` — not awaited, no catch; called from toggleEnabled (:104), handleTimeChange (:111), handleAddReminder (:117), confirmDelete (:125); handleBannerPress (:92) and ReminderPromptHost.tsx:65 call it the same way. app/_layout.tsx:169-171 starts another run at launch, also un-awaited and without `.catch`.
findings.goesWrong: User toggles reminder A on and within ~100 ms changes reminder B's time (or opens the Reminders screen and toggles right after cold start while the startup sync is still running). Interleaving: run1 cancelAll → run2 cancelAll → run1 schedules A,B → run2 schedules A,B → every reminder fires twice daily. Because no notification ids are persisted, nothing detects this; it only self-heals at the next sync. Separately, any rejection (e.g. a malformed `time` producing NaN hour → scheduleNotificationAsync validation error) is an unhandled promise rejection: silent in release, reminders simply stop being scheduled.
findings.fix: Serialize syncs through a module-level promise chain (`let chain = Promise.resolve(); export function syncReminderNotifications(...) { chain = chain.then(() => doSync(...)).catch(err => recordError(err, 'reminder sync failed')); return chain; }`) or debounce to the latest DB state. Add `.catch(recordError)` at both call sites.

findings.title: Reminder sync is cancel-all-then-reschedule with no serialisation; overlapping toggles can leave a disabled reminder scheduled
findings.eli5: Same as A111: flipping a reminder on and off fast can leave it scheduled even though it shows as off. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: syncReminderNotifications (cancel-all then per-reminder schedule, no serialisation or generation guard) is fired without await/catch from reminders.tsx refreshAndSync and _layout.tsx launch; overlapping runs can interleave so an earlier run's schedule lands after a later run's cancel-all, leaving a reminder the UI shows as off (or a stale time) scheduled, and the launch sync skips cleanup when no reminder is enabled. Native rejections are unhandled.
findings.evidence: notifications.ts:117 `await Notifications.cancelAllScheduledNotificationsAsync();` followed by one awaited `scheduleNotificationAsync` per enabled reminder (:122-132). reminders.tsx:51-54 `function refreshAndSync(next) { setReminders(next); syncReminderNotifications(next, t); }` — not awaited, not caught, no in-flight guard; also started from _layout.tsx:100-102 on launch.
findings.goesWrong: User flips a reminder on and immediately off (double tap on the Switch). Run A (enabled list) awaits cancelAll; run B (disabled list) awaits cancelAll; A resumes and schedules the reminder daily; B has nothing to schedule. The UI shows the reminder off but it fires at the chosen time every day until the next sync. Any rejection from the native scheduler is an unhandled promise rejection with no user feedback.
findings.fix: Serialise syncs through a single promise chain (e.g. `syncQueue = syncQueue.then(() => doSync(...))`) and compute the reminder list inside the queued task from the DB rather than from the caller's snapshot, so the last write wins; await and catch in callers (recordError + StatusDialog).

findings.title: 'Generated' date in the PDF is the UTC date, not the user's local date
findings.eli5: The 'Generated' date on the PDF uses UTC, so in some time zones it shows yesterday's or tomorrow's date. Fixed on 11 November 2026.

findings.title: `Animated.event` and the interpolation nodes are rebuilt on every render of the host screen

findings.fix: Wrap `onScroll` and the three interpolations in `useMemo(() => ..., [scrollY])` (or build them once in the same `useRef` initializer as `scrollY`).

findings.title: withEnglishMetadata throws at module-evaluation time and only guards one direction of drift
findings.eli5: If a Learn article's identifier is mistyped in one language, the whole Learn screen crashes instead of showing a fallback. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: withEnglishMetadata (content.ts:44-50) throws when a translated slug has no English counterpart, but it is now called lazily from getLearnArticles() (:86-90) on every render of the Learn index/article screens rather than at module scope, so a slug typo in one of the 27 translated article files would crash the Learn screens (unhandled throw during render) instead of failing app startup; the reverse drift (English article missing from a locale) is still not detected or back-filled, leaving that locale with a shorter list and 'learn.notFound' for the slug. All 28 locales currently carry the same 8 slugs, so this is latent, not an active bug. getLearnArticles is also re-run (and the arrays re-mapped) on every render since nothing is memoised.
findings.evidence: content.ts:44-50 — `function withEnglishMetadata(copy) { return copy.map(article => { const source = en.find(item => item.slug === article.slug); if (!source) throw new Error(`Missing English Learn article: ${article.slug}`); … }) }`; :86-90 — `export function getLearnArticles(locale?) { if (!locale) return en; const copy = localized[locale] ?? localized[locale.split('-')[0]]; return copy ? withEnglishMetadata(copy) : en; }`; called from app/learn/[slug].tsx:19 and app/learn/index.tsx in render. No check that every English slug is present in each translation; `grep -c 'slug:' src/features/learn/articles/*.ts` → 8 for all 28 files; package.json has no test script.
findings.goesWrong: A future edit renames an English slug (e.g. 'medicines' → 'medications') but not the Spanish one: the throw fires during route-module loading and the whole app fails to start, not just the Learn screen. Conversely, if the next article is added to `en` only, Spanish/French/German users silently get one guide fewer and `learn.updated`/the review package never notice.
findings.fix: Make the mismatch a dev-only warning plus fallback to the English article (so a content typo can't take the app down), add the reverse check (every English slug present in each locale, falling back to the English article when missing), and cover it with the existing tests/ folder once a runner exists.

findings.title: `impact` is declared INTEGER but holds a TEXT enum; legacy integer rows survive every reader invisibly
findings.eli5: The 'impact' column had the wrong type in the database. Fixed.
findings.what: `entries.impact` is declared INTEGER but the app writes/reads the string enum manageable|bothersome|distressing (types.ts:51); no migration or CHECK exists, so a legacy numeric value (dev-era seed or an imported backup — importEntries at queries.ts:345 inserts impact unvalidated, and INTEGER affinity coerces "3" to 3) is hidden by display paths (ExpandableEntryRow.tsx:155 '—', trends.tsx:923 excluded) yet counted as a detailed check-in (evaluate.ts:142) and silently re-persisted by the edit screen ([id].tsx:199 → updateEntry). Dormant hazard only: no store/EAS build (eas.json from 2026-05-21) predates the enum change (bc8d47e, 2026-05-17).
findings.evidence: app/db/database.ts:34 `impact     INTEGER,` vs app/db/types.ts:51 `impact: Distress | null;`. Commit bc8d47e (2026-05-17, "change distress from 1-5 scale to manageable/bothersome/distressing") changed only types/queries/seed/UI — database.ts diff touches only seedDevData. Readers today: app/components/ExpandableEntryRow.tsx:155 `const distressValid = entry.impact === 'manageable' || ...` renders '—' for a number; app/(tabs)/trends.tsx:923 `if (val !== null && counts.has(val))` drops it from the Distress card; but app/entry/[id].tsx:199 `setImpact(entry.impact)` feeds the number into `SegmentedControl` ([id].tsx:105 `value === opt.value` never matches) and Save writes it back via updateEntry; src/features/achievements/evaluate.ts:142 counts `e.impact !== null` as a detailed check-in; app/my-data.tsx:147 exports `impact: e.impact` raw and app/db/queries.ts:345 re-inserts `e.impact ?? null` with no type check. Git grounding: the numeric-impact entry form existed only between f1b5183 (2026-04-29) and bc8d47e (2026-05-17); eas.json first appeared at f8ba705 (2026-05-21) and the 1.0.1 bump at c30bf6d (2026-05-24), both after the enum change, and `android/` is untracked — so no store/EAS build ever wrote integer impact.
findings.goesWrong: A dev-era database (or a backup exported from one) has a row with impact=3. Home/Calendar show Distress '—', Stats Distress card excludes it from its total, yet Milestones counts the entry as 'detailed' and opening it in the edit screen shows no distress selected while Save silently persists 3 again; a backup carrying `"impact": "3"` is coerced to INTEGER 3 by the column's affinity on import. Because this shape never shipped in a store build this is a schema/type mismatch with dormant hazard, not user data loss.
findings.fix: Either migrate in initDatabase (`UPDATE entries SET impact = CASE impact WHEN 1 THEN 'manageable' WHEN 2 THEN 'manageable' WHEN 3 THEN 'bothersome' WHEN 4 THEN 'distressing' WHEN 5 THEN 'distressing' END WHERE typeof(impact)='integer'`, or NULL them) and document the column as TEXT, or at minimum have importEntries/updateEntry reject non-enum values so the mismatch cannot be re-introduced. Add a CHECK on new installs.

findings.title: Reminder notifications can be (re)scheduled in English at cold start and are never re-synced after a language change
findings.eli5: Same as A37: reminder notifications are not re-translated after you change the app language. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: `setLanguage` (LanguageContext.tsx:97-100) never calls `syncReminderNotifications`, and the other sync sites are the Reminders screen (reminders.tsx:92/:98), the reminder soft-ask (ReminderPromptHost.tsx:65) and the cold-start sync (_layout.tsx:170); so after a language change, already-scheduled reminder notifications keep their old-language title/body until a reminder is next edited or a later cold start happens to run the sync after `LanguageProvider`'s `changeLanguage` effect. Additionally, because i18n is initialised with `lng: 'en'` (i18n/index.ts:70) and the real language is only applied in a post-mount effect (LanguageContext.tsx:90-95), the cold-start sync's `t()` (evaluated after two native round trips) can race that effect and schedule reminders in English on slower devices.
findings.evidence: app/i18n/index.ts:70 `lng: 'en'` (saved/device language not consulted at init). app/contexts/LanguageContext.tsx:90-95 `useEffect(() => { i18n.changeLanguage(resolvedLanguage); setPurchasesLocale(resolvedLanguage); }, [resolvedLanguage])` — runs only after providers mount, which happens after `setAppReady(true)` (app/_layout.tsx:174, :180-189). app/_layout.tsx:169-171 `hasNotificationPermission().then(granted => { if (granted) syncReminderNotifications(reminders, i18n.t.bind(i18n)); })` — `t()` is evaluated inside the sync after another native round trip (`await cancelAll...`, notifications.ts:156, then :163-164). `setLanguage` (LanguageContext.tsx:97-100) does not call syncReminderNotifications; WidgetSync (_layout.tsx:97) listens to `languageChanged` but only refreshes widgets.
findings.goesWrong: Deterministic part: German user has the daily reminder on, switches Settings > Language from English to Deutsch → the 20:00 notification keeps the English title/body until they next touch the Reminders screen. Race part: on a slower device the startup sync's `t()` runs before LanguageProvider's `changeLanguage`, rewriting every reminder to English on each cold start even though the app UI is German. The same ordering also means the first painted frame after the splash hides (SafeAreaProvider onLayout, :114) can be in English before flipping.
findings.fix: Resolve the language synchronously before the first render: read the saved `language` setting / `resolveAutomaticLanguage()` inside the startup effect and call `i18n.changeLanguage` before `setAppReady(true)` (or compute `lng` in app/i18n/index.ts from the setting). Then call `syncReminderNotifications(getReminders(), t)` (permission permitting) from the LanguageProvider effect or `setLanguage` so scheduled text follows the UI language.

findings.title: SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and legacy external-storage permissions ship because app.json never blocks Expo's optional defaults
findings.eli5: The Android app still asks for a 'draw over other apps' permission and old storage permissions it never uses, which looks bad in the Play Store listing. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: app.json's `android.blockedPermissions` (lines 33-37) only blocks the three advertising-ID permissions, so prebuild still ships Expo's optional template defaults — SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW plus READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (the latter maxSdkVersion=32, inert on Android 13+) — even though the app only uses SAF, MediaStore Downloads, DocumentPicker-to-cache and cache files, which need none of them.
findings.evidence: app.json:33-37 `"blockedPermissions": ["com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID", "android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION", "android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID"]` — no SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW or storage entries. Source of the defaults: node_modules/@expo/config-plugins/build/plugins/withAndroidBaseMods.js:62-66 (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE maxSdkVersion=32) and node_modules/expo-file-system/plugin/build/withFileSystem.js:8-9 adding the storage pair; the (stale, Aug-11) local android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:3-6 shows them declared. File I/O in the app is MediaStore (my-data.tsx:106-118), SAF (:121-128), DocumentPicker with copyToCacheDirectory (:293) and cache files (:257, reportExport.ts:12-19).
findings.goesWrong: Play Console lists 'Display over other apps' and storage permissions for a health diary that never requests them; SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW in particular is a flagged permission in Play policy reviews and in third-party security scanners, and it is only meaningful for the RN dev error overlay. Note the local manifest is a stale Aug-11 prebuild (it predates expo-notifications/local-authentication/Firebase and lacks POST_NOTIFICATIONS, USE_BIOMETRIC, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED), so it cannot be used as the release reference; the fix belongs in app.json.
findings.fix: Add `"android": { "blockedPermissions": ["android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW", "android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE", "android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE"] }` to app.json and re-run prebuild; then review the regenerated manifest (not the stale one) before the next release.

findings.title: Android auto-backup is left on (Expo default), so the SQLite health diary is uploaded to Google Drive outside the App Lock
findings.eli5: Android was backing up the unencrypted diary to Google Drive by default. Fixed: automatic backup is off.
findings.what: `expo.android` in app.json sets no `allowBackup`, so the Expo config plugin defaults the generated (gitignored) AndroidManifest to `android:allowBackup="true"` with no `fullBackupContent`/`dataExtractionRules`; the whole private data dir, including the SQLite health diary `tinnitus.db` and the `settings` table, is included in Google auto-backup regardless of App Lock, which only gates the UI.
findings.evidence: AndroidManifest.xml:14 `android:allowBackup="true"`; node_modules/@expo/config-plugins/build/android/AllowBackup.js:26 `return config.android?.allowBackup ?? true;`; app.json:18-28 has no `allowBackup` key. The DB is a plain file opened at database.ts:4 `SQLite.openDatabaseSync('tinnitus.db')`; App Lock only gates the UI (app/_layout.tsx:61) and the app describes itself as local-first with an explicit, user-driven export (my-data.tsx).
findings.goesWrong: A user who enables App Lock and never exports still has their entries, notes and `settings` (name, app_lock_enabled, export_dir_uri) copied to their Google account's device backup and restored onto any device signed into that account, which is a different data flow than the one the My Data screen presents.
findings.fix: Decide explicitly: either set `"android": { "allowBackup": false }` in app.json (matching the local-first/App Lock story and the manual export path), or keep it on and add a `fullBackupContent`/`dataExtractionRules` XML that excludes `databases/` and `files/SQLite` while allowing preferences. Either way it should be a recorded decision rather than the template default.

findings.eli5: Partly fixed. Same as A52: on iPhone, export and import leave plain-text copies of the diary in a temporary folder, and export is recorded as done even if cancelled.

findings.title: Calibration study reports FAIL but always exits 0

'did not overclaim' : 'overclaimed'}`; there is no `process.exit(1)` or thrown error anywhere in the file (unlike the two .validation.ts files, whose `assert` throws). findings.title: Saved language is applied in a passive effect after the first commit, so the first painted frame is English

findings.title: Reminder is enabled and scheduled before the permission prompt; a denial leaves the switch on with nothing that can fire
findings.eli5: Partly fixed. If you turn on a reminder and then deny the notification permission, the switch stays on even though nothing can ever fire.

Since 2026-11-09 the screen does surface this — an inline 'Notifications are off' banner with Allow/Open settings (:58, :141-154, re-checked on every AppState 'active' at :68-74) and a StatusDialog when the OS is blocked (:82) — but the toggle is never reverted, and app/_layout.tsx:169-171 still silently skips the launch sync when permission is absent, so the on-state persists until the user acts on the banner.
findings.evidence: app/reminders.tsx:101-107 `updateReminder(reminder.id, { enabled: enabling }); refreshAndSync(getReminders()); ... if (enabling) await requestPermissionForReminder();` — no revert of the toggle; :79-83 `requestPermissionForReminder` only sets `permissionBlocked` when `state === 'blocked'`. :58 `showPermissionBanner = permission !== null && permission !== 'granted' && reminders.some(r => r.enabled === 1)`; :68-74 refreshes on AppState 'active'. app/_layout.tsx:169-171 skips the sync on later launches when permission is absent.

findings.title: Linking.openURL rejections are unhandled on five screens, so buttons silently do nothing without a mail/browser app
findings.eli5: Same as A53: 'Contact support' and other links fail silently if there is no mail app or browser. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: Linking.openURL is fire-and-forget on seven call sites (support.tsx:54, support-directory.tsx:137, connect.tsx:43, about.tsx:14, learn/[slug].tsx:66, (tabs)/more.tsx:116, components/UsageConsentScreen.tsx:65), so when no handler app exists (most plausibly no mail client for the mailto: links) the promise rejects silently and the button does nothing, contradicting the "It'll open your mail app" copy; support-directory.tsx:66-72 already has the try/catch + StatusDialog pattern to reuse.
findings.evidence: support.tsx:54 `Linking.openURL(url);` (mailto). Also connect.tsx:43 `onPress={() => Linking.openURL(link.url)}`, about.tsx:14 `const openUrl = (url: string) => () => Linking.openURL(url);`, learn/[slug].tsx:66, (tabs)/more.tsx:116 `Linking.openURL(managementUrl ?? PLAY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_URL);`, support-directory.tsx:137 for its own mailto, and UsageConsentScreen.tsx:65 `Linking.openURL(PRIVACY_POLICY_URL)` (onboarding privacy step and the one-time consent screen). Contrast support-directory.tsx:66-72 `try { await Linking.openURL(item.url); } catch { setLinkError(true); }`. All targets are hard-coded https:/mailto: constants, so this is not a scheme-injection issue.
findings.goesWrong: On an Android device with no email client (work profile, de-Googled phone, emulator) the user taps 'Contact support'; the promise rejects, nothing visible happens, and the support copy ('It'll open your mail app...') is contradicted. In dev this shows as an unhandled-promise warning; in production it is just a dead button.
findings.fix: Create one `openExternal(url)` helper that awaits openURL, catches, and surfaces the existing `localSupport.openErrorTitle/Body` style dialog (or a toast); use it on all six call sites. For mailto, consider showing the address so it can be copied when no client exists.

findings.title: Android backs up the unencrypted symptom database to Google Drive by default
findings.eli5: Same as A157: the diary was being backed up to Google Drive unencrypted. Fixed.
findings.what: `app.json` sets no `android.allowBackup`; Expo's default is `true`: "Allows your user's app data to be automatically backed up to their Google Drive… set to false… if your app deals with sensitive information" ([Expo config reference](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/config/app/)). The DB is plain SQLite (`app/db/database.ts:4`). Under GDPR Art. 4(15) a tinnitus diary is "data concerning health" whatever the product positioning ([Art. 4 GDPR](https://gdpr-info.eu/art-4-gdpr/)), so this is a silent off-device transfer the policy denies ("stored locally on your device"). Set `"android": { "allowBackup": false }` or disclose it. App Lock protects the UI only, not the file.

findings.title: "Wellness, not health" is only partly true, and one planned feature would break it
findings.eli5: Still open as a process item. The app is positioned as 'wellness, not medical', which holds as long as it never diagnoses or measures. The planned Pitch Test (which would have crossed that line) was removed; a short regulatory memo is still to write.
findings.what:
- GDPR: the data *is* health data (see #6); positioning changes nothing there. Local-only storage is what keeps this manageable — keep it that way and say so.
- US: FDA's general-wellness safe harbour requires software "unrelated to the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition" ([FDA General Wellness guidance](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/general-wellness-policy-low-risk-devices)). A tinnitus-named symptom diary is not in that bucket; it relies instead on being a low-risk record-keeping tool. That holds as long as the app does not measure, diagnose or recommend treatment.
- The "Pitch Test — Identify your tinnitus frequency" row is no longer rendered on the More tab (`app/(tabs)/more.tsx:174-175` keeps only a comment: hidden until it exists), but the strings still ship in every locale (`en.json:176-177`) and `openPaywall` still accepts a 'pitch_test' feature, so the plan is alive. It is a measurement claim: Google says "Apps performing diagnosis, treatment recommendations, or clinical monitoring may qualify as Software as a Medical Device" ([Play Health apps policy](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/12991134)); Apple 1.4.1 rejects unvalidated measurement claims. Decide the regulatory position before building it, or drop the strings.
- Trigger Impact is the closest existing feature to "providing information for medical decisions"; its framing as association with explicit uncertainty (`en.json:125` "ASSOCIATION, NOT CAUSE", `src/features/statistics/guides/en.ts:11,61`, PDF disclaimer `en.json:354`) is the right defence. Keep that wording under change control.
findings.evidence: app/(tabs)/more.tsx:174-175 `{/* Pitch Test is hidden until it exists: a Pro badge on a 'coming soon' screen would sell a feature the subscription doesn't deliver. */}` with no row following; en.json:176-177 `"pitchTest": "Pitch Test", "pitchTestSubtitle": "Identify your tinnitus frequency"`; en.json:125 trigger info text contains `ASSOCIATION, NOT CAUSE\nThese are patterns in what you logged. They cannot prove a trigger caused anything.`; src/features/statistics/guides/en.ts:11 'The results describe associations in your diary. They do not prove that a trigger caused a change.', :61 '7. Association is not causation'; en.json:354 PDF `"disclaimer": "... Associations do not prove that a trigger caused a change and the report is not a diagnosis or treatment recommendation ..."`.

findings.title: Accessibility
findings.eli5: Buttons had no screen-reader names and text contrast was too low. No longer applies: both were fixed.
findings.what: Only 1 `accessibilityLabel` across 99 `PressableScale` uses; the 28 icon-only back buttons (e.g. `app/about.tsx:64–66`) announce nothing to TalkBack/VoiceOver. Contrast (computed): `textMuted #94A3B8` on white = **2.56:1**, `textFaint #CBD5E1` = **1.48:1** (`app/constants/theme.ts:100–101`); WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for body text, and `textMuted` is used in 75 places, often at 11–13 px (e.g. `app/about.tsx:262–267`). Dark theme is better but `textMuted` still 3.73:1. The European Accessibility Act applies to consumer apps selling services in the EU since June 2025 ([Directive 2019/882](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj)).

findings.title: RevenueCat receives the Firebase app instance id at startup, before usage-data consent

findings.title: Firebase Performance uploads traces without consent: perf_auto_collection_enabled is not set
findings.eli5: Firebase Performance (timing measurements) is still sent to Google regardless of your consent choice; only Analytics and Crashlytics respect it. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: firebase.json disables auto-collection only for Analytics and Crashlytics (:4-5). perf_auto_collection_enabled is absent and nothing calls setPerformanceCollectionEnabled, so Firebase Performance starts natively on launch and the traces started in app/my-data.tsx:28 are uploaded for every user, including those who declined. google_analytics_adid_collection_enabled is also unset (low impact, AD_ID is blocked).
findings.evidence: firebase.json:4-5 contains analytics_auto_collection_enabled:false and crashlytics_auto_collection_enabled:false only; `grep -rn setPerformanceCollectionEnabled app src` → no hits; app/utils/performance.ts never reads usage_data_consent.
findings.goesWrong: Telemetry still leaves the device for users who said no, so L2 is only partly closed and the Play Data safety form cannot state that collection is optional.
findings.fix: Add "perf_auto_collection_enabled": false (and "google_analytics_adid_collection_enabled": false) to firebase.json; in consent.ts call perf().setPerformanceCollectionEnabled(consent) next to the Analytics and Crashlytics toggles.

findings.title: Lock screen has no BackHandler: Android Back reaches the navigator underneath while locked
findings.eli5: With the app locked, pressing the Android Back button still controls the hidden screens underneath the lock. Fixed on 11 November 2026.
findings.what: The lock screen is rendered as an absolute-fill overlay above the Stack (app/_layout.tsx:137-138). LockScreen.tsx registers no BackHandler, so the hardware Back button while locked pops screens or exits the app underneath the overlay.
findings.evidence: `grep -n BackHandler app/components/LockScreen.tsx` → nothing; app/_layout.tsx:137-138 `{locked && <LockScreen style={StyleSheet.absoluteFill} />}` after the Stack.

findings.fix: In LockScreen, add a BackHandler.addEventListener("hardwareBackPress", () => true) while locked (and consider accessibilityViewIsModal / importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" on the Stack underneath).

findings.title: Reminder toggle schedules the notification before the permission request and never re-syncs after permission is granted

On iOS a request added before authorization is rejected (notificationsNotAllowed), so after the user taps Allow nothing is scheduled until the next cold start (_layout.tsx:167-172). `handleBannerPress` (:85-94) and `ReminderPromptHost.accept` do it in the right order.

findings.fix: In requestPermissionForReminder: `if (granted) syncReminderNotifications(getReminders(), t)`; add a .catch to the fire-and-forget sync calls.

findings.title: formatSigned prints "−0.0"/"+0.0" for values that round to zero
findings.what: formatSigned() takes the sign from the unrounded value and the magnitude from formatNumber() (format.ts:30-35), so −0.04 becomes "−0.0" and +0.04 "+0.0". It replaced the toFixed-based caption that A102 flagged for the same reason ("-0%"), and is now used for the Change tiles on Home and Stats, every trigger effect, the interval bounds and the day-before/after tiles.
findings.evidence: format.ts:30-35 `const abs = formatNumber(Math.abs(value), digits); if (value > 0) return `+${abs}`; if (value < 0) return `\u2212${abs}`; return abs;` — no rounding before the sign test.
findings.goesWrong: A week whose average moved by 0.03 levels shows "−0.0 levels" on the Change tile, coloured as a change (levelTextColor treats |v| < 0.2 as neutral, so the colour says "no change" while the sign says "down").
findings.fix: Round first: `const r = Number(value.toFixed(digits))` (or compare `Math.abs(value) < 0.5 * 10 ** -digits`) and sign on r; return abs for r === 0.

history.note: Found by quality scan at ab20712

findings.eli5: Still open. A change so small it rounds to zero can show as "−0.0" with a minus sign, which looks like a drop when nothing really changed.
